skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Automates browser interactions for web testing, form filling, screenshots, video capture, authentication flows, and page data extraction.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents through repeatable browser automation with the agent-browser CLI.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples for the allowed agent-browser CLI and were false positives for command execution. Confirmed issues involve proxy routing, SOCKS support, explicit proxy rotation to avoid rate limits or bans, persistent authentication state files, and one active screenshot write to /tmp. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Proxy rotation guidance can enable anti-abuse circumvention.
remediation.suggestion: Remove language about avoiding rate limits or bans, and limit proxy examples to authorized testing, corporate access, or compliance checks.

remediation.issue: Proxy examples include credential-bearing URLs and broad proxy environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Use redacted placeholders and recommend secret managers or environment variables that do not expose credentials in shell history.

remediation.issue: Authenticated state files contain session tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the warning prominent, add restrictive file-permission guidance, and recommend deletion after each task or CI run.

remediation.issue: A workflow template writes screenshots to a fixed /tmp path.
remediation.suggestion: Write artifacts to a user-selected private output directory and avoid predictable temporary filenames for sensitive screenshots.

content.value_statement: Web testing and content capture often require many fragile browser steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable agent-browser workflow.
actual_capabilities: Open pages, take snapshots, and interact with elements through stable @ref references.
Fill forms, click controls, select options, upload files, and wait for page states.
Capture screenshots, PDFs, videos, console messages, and page error details.
Manage sessions, cookies, local storage, authentication state, viewport, device, headers, and geolocation.
Use workflow templates for forms, authenticated sessions, and content capture.
limitations: Requires the agent-browser CLI to be installed and available to the AI tool.
Can only access sites and sessions that the local browser environment can reach.
Element references can become stale after navigation or dynamic page updates.
Authenticated state and screenshots may contain private data and need careful storage.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable checks for login, checkout, forms, and responsive page behavior.

use_cases.title: Debug Frontend Issues
use_cases.description: Inspect page state, console output, screenshots, and recordings while reproducing UI bugs.

use_cases.title: Capture Web Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect page text, screenshots, PDFs, and workflow recordings for documentation or audits.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL with agent-browser, take an interactive snapshot, and summarize the visible primary actions.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to inspect this form, fill safe test values, submit it, and report validation or success states.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Authenticated Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Load the saved browser state, open the protected page, capture a screenshot and PDF, then clear sensitive session data.

prompt_templates.title: Record and Diagnose a Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Record the browser workflow, reproduce the failing interaction, collect console errors, and provide a concise diagnosis.

output_examples.input: A QA engineer asks to verify a checkout form.
output: The assistant identifies the form controls, fills safe test values, submits the form, and reports the observed result.
The response includes key validation messages and whether the expected confirmation appeared.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to reproduce a visual bug on mobile.
output: The assistant sets the mobile viewport, opens the page, captures a screenshot, and lists visible layout problems.
The response notes console errors and the page area where the issue appears.

output_examples.input: A writer asks for evidence from a product page.
output: The assistant captures the page title, visible main content, a full-page screenshot, and a PDF.
The response summarizes where each artifact was saved and what content was visible.

best_practices: Take a fresh interactive snapshot before each important interaction.
Use test accounts and avoid storing real credentials in prompts or files.
Delete screenshots, recordings, and authentication state when they are no longer needed.
anti_patterns: Using stale element references after navigation or major DOM changes.
Automating third-party sites without permission or against their terms.
Saving authenticated state, screenshots, or recordings in shared temporary paths.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, page inspection, form interaction, screenshots, PDFs, video recording, and session handling.

faq.question: Does it require a separate tool?
faq.answer: Yes. The local agent-browser CLI must be installed and allowed by the AI tool.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents saved browser state, cookies, and credentials, but these files can contain sensitive session tokens.

faq.question: Can it record browser sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports WebM recordings for debugging, documentation, and test evidence.

faq.question: Is proxy support included?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxy configuration, which must be used only for authorized testing.

faq.question: What should users avoid?
faq.answer: Avoid storing private data in shared paths, scraping without permission, and reusing stale element references.
